backup.production_rule: Privacy fix. public.guest_context_v1(uuid, uuid, text) is SECURITY DEFINER with no auth check and authenticated could execute it (production read 2026-11-18; anon could not, service_role could), so any signed-in user could read a guest's private fields (stay count, last issue, preferences, tags, VIP reason, note, birthday, open follow-ups) by name. The migration revokes all from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role and grants execute to service_role only, then reads the ACL back and raises (55000) unless only the owner and service_role appear in it. No body, signature, owner or search_path change; no table or data written. Callers found in the current app repos on 2026-11-18: the edge functions airbnb-email-sync, submit-booking, telegram-cassy and guest-reply-draft, through _shared/cascade-core/tools.ts, all with a service-role client; no front end and no SQL function calls it. Before the apply, read production once more: select p.proname from pg_proc p where p.prosrc ilike '%guest_context_v1%' and p.proname <> 'guest_context_v1' (expect no rows), and stop if a user-token caller turns up.
backup.notes: Narrowing grant only, so it is the one SQL step of this release; no deploy needed because every caller already uses the service role. Does not depend on the usage-learning or guest-count releases. Reversal reopens the read to signed-in users: only if an app that calls it with a user token is found, and then fix that caller.

forward_verification.name: function_still_security_definer
forward_verification.query: select prosecdef from pg_proc where oid = 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)'::regprocedure

forward_verification.name: only_service_role_can_execute
forward_verification.query: select has_function_privilege('service_role', 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('authenticated', 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)', 'execute')

forward_verification.name: acl_names_only_owner_and_service_role
forward_verification.query: select (select p.proacl is not null from pg_proc p where p.oid = 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)'::regprocedure) and not exists (select 1 from pg_proc p cross join lateral aclexplode(p.proacl) a where p.oid = 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)'::regprocedure and a.grantee <> p.proowner and a.grantee <> (select r.oid from pg_roles r where r.rolname = 'service_role'))

rollback.safe_until: Always, with the privacy exposure by design: it puts the grants of migration 20260916160000 back (revoked from PUBLIC and anon, execute for service_role and authenticated), which lets every signed-in user read the private guest fields again. Use it only if an app that calls the function with a user token is found.

steps.name: run_compensating_script
steps.action: apply supabase/rollbacks/20261120_s120_guest_context_grant.sql with run-sql-on-host.sh; then has_function_privilege('authenticated', 'public.guest_context_v1(uuid,uuid,text)', 'execute') must be true and the same for anon false.

feature_flags.name: no_flag_no_app_change
feature_flags.required_state: None. Every caller of guest_context_v1 uses the service role; no app or edge function is changed or redeployed.

Log docs/s120/rehearsal-all-3.log, run at f05351e. This release's migration, rollback and suite are unchanged since the commit named in source.commit (later commits only touch s120_count_learning).

the restore point is older than one hour, or restore_point / verified_at are still the placeholders
